title: Past Halfway in Both Directions
surface: I travel the same road between home and work. Whenever I look through the vehicle window at my friend’s house, I think, “More than halfway now.” This is true in both directions. The house stays put and the route never changes. How?
solution: The house is near the route’s midpoint. In either direction I wait until we have passed that midpoint, then look back through a side window. The moment I see the house is therefore after halfway on either trip. Seeing a house need not mean just arriving beside it.

facts.text: The house is near the midpoint of the fixed route.
In both directions the traveler looks back at it only after passing the midpoint.
The endpoints and route never change, and there is no detour.

unknowns: The distance, vehicle and delay before looking back are unspecified.
hints: Must seeing and passing the house happen together?
A window can show more than the road ahead.
Both times, the traveler has passed the midpoint before looking back.
